title: NFTMigrator.migrate() DoS when a V1 index has no V2 mapping
description: `setInitialized()` checks that every V1 index in `[1, v1.nextIndex())` has a non-zero mapping, but this check is not re-performed at migration time. If the V1 owner registers a new V1 dispatcher **after** initialization, that new V1 index has no V2 mapping. The `migrate()` loop iterates from 1 up to the live `v1.nextIndex()`; upon reaching the unmapped index it calls `v2.mintFor(0, msg.sender)` which reverts with "NFTMinterV2: index not registered", aborting the entire tx. Users holding NFTs at the unmapped index cannot migrate any of their V1 NFTs.
impact: Migration availability failure. Users whose V1 portfolio includes any post-init V1 index are effectively locked out of migrating.
attack_path: Non-malicious owner registers a V1 dispatcher after calling migrator.setInitialized().
Every user who holds at least one NFT in the new V1 index has their migration revert.
Not exploitable for profit; pure availability risk.
recommendation: In `migrate()`, skip indexes where `indexMapping[i] == 0` (or explicitly revert early with a clear error). Optionally freeze V1 dispatcher registration via a lock controlled by the migrator after init.
